Cardamom Milk (Elaichi Doodh)

Served at: Gita Jayanti (गीता जयंती)

Serves 2Prep 5 minCook 10 min

Cardamom Milk, or Elaichi Doodh, is a fragrant and comforting beverage often prepared during Hindu festivals and spiritual occasions. For Gita Jayanti, it serves as a soothing offering to Lord Krishna and a gentle, warming drink for devotees reflecting on the profound teachings of the Bhagavad Gita.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (470 ml) whole milk
  • 4 green cardamom pods, lightly crushed, or 1/2 teaspoon ground cardamom
  • 2 tablespoons (25 g) granulated sugar, or to taste
  • A few strands of saffron (optional, for garnish)

Method

  1. Pour the milk into a small saucepan.
  2. Add the lightly crushed green cardamom pods (or ground cardamom) to the milk.
  3. Place the saucepan over medium heat and bring the milk to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally to prevent scorching.
  4. Once simmering, reduce the heat to low and let it cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing the cardamom flavor to infuse into the milk.
  5. Stir in the granulated sugar until it completely dissolves.
  6. Remove the saucepan from the heat.
  7. If using whole cardamom pods, strain the milk through a fine-mesh sieve into serving cups to remove the pods.
  8. Garnish with a few strands of saffron, if desired, and serve warm.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, you can use full-fat milk. Dairy-free alternatives like almond or oat milk also work well.
  • Adjust the amount of sugar to your preference; some prefer it less sweet, especially when offered as prasad.
  • This milk can also be enjoyed chilled. Prepare it in advance and refrigerate for a refreshing treat.
